item.title: [CRITICAL] rancher/rancher — Unauthenticated update of public UI settings leading to stored cross-site scripting in Rancher (CVE-2026-88804)
item.description:
CVE-2026-88804 · CVSS 9.4 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:H/SI:H/SA:H) · CWE-79, CWE-862
Affected: - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=v2.15.0, <v2.15.2 (patched: v2.15.2) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=v2.14.0, <v2.14.6 (patched: v2.14.6) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=v2.13.0, <v2.13.10 (patched: v2.13.10) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=v2.12.0, <v2.12.14 (patched: v2.12.14) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=v2.11.0, <v2.11.18 (patched: v2.11.18)
---
### Impact
A security vulnerability exists in the Rancher Manager API routes that serve a small set of public UI settings without authentication. These routes were intended to be read-only, but a request-parsing behavior in the underlying Norman API framework allowed a remote, unauthenticated user with network access to the Rancher server to modify the values of those public settings.
Because one of these settings is rendered as raw HTML on the Rancher login page, an unauthenticated attacker could persist attacker-controlled content that is then executed in the browser of any user who opens the login page, in the Rancher origin. This can lead to disclosure of the local administrator bootstrap password or hijacking of an active administrator session, and therefore to full administrative control of the Rancher installation and of the downstream clusters it manages.
#### Preconditions
- The attacker requires network access to the Rancher server endpoint. No Rancher account, credentials, or prior privileges are required. - A legitimate user must subsequently open the Rancher login page for the stored content to take effect. No other deliberate action from that user is required.
> [!NOTE] > Deployments in a default configuration are affected; no non-default feature or setting needs to be enabled.
### Patches
The fix hardens the unauthenticated Rancher API router so that the public settings endpoints are strictly read-only. Request parameters that could reinterpret the effective HTTP method of a request are now stripped before the request reaches the management API handler, so requests to these unauthenticated routes can no longer result in a write to a setting.
The change is server-side only and does not alter the values or behavior of the settings themselves, so no user action beyond upgrading is required.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases v2.15.2, v2.14.6, v2.13.10, v2.12.14, and v2.11.18.
Administrators who suspect their installation was targeted before upgrading should review the current values of the public UI settings (for example `ui-pl`, `first-login`, `ui-banners`, `ui-brand`, `ui-issues`, and `ui-default-landing`) and restore any unexpected values, rotate the local administrator password, and invalidate existing administrator tokens and sessions.
### Workarounds
No workaround fully addresses the issue other than upgrading to a patched version. Users who cannot upgrade immediately can reduce exposure by:
- Restricting network access to the Rancher server endpoint to trusted networks and clients. - Placing Rancher behind a reverse proxy, WAF, or ingress policy that rejects requests to the unauthenticated `/v3/settings/*` endpoints carrying HTTP method-override parameters or request bodies, allowing only plain read requests. - Monitoring the values of the public UI settings listed above for unexpected changes.
### Credits
This vulnerability was discovered and reported by [@StopWar](https://x.com/st0pw4r).
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
- Reach out to the [SUSE Rancher Security team](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/policy) for security related inquiries. - Open an issue in the [Rancher](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/new/choose) repository. - Verify our [support matrix](https://www.suse.com/suse-rancher/support-matrix/all-supported-versions/) and [product support life cycle](https://www.suse.com/lifecycle/).

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/rancher — Session Not Revoked Server-Side on Logout in Rancher (CVE-2026-88805)
item.description:
CVE-2026-88805 · CVSS 7.4 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:A/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-287, CWE-613
Affected: - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=v2.15.0, <v2.15.2 (patched: v2.15.2)
---
### Impact
A session revocation vulnerability exists in Rancher's logout handling for public API session tokens. When a user logs out of the Rancher UI, the browser session cookies are cleared, but the corresponding server-side session token is not removed from its backing store. As a result, the session token remains valid and continues to authenticate API requests until its configured time-to-live or idle timeout expires.
Logout is the primary control available to users and administrators to immediately terminate a session that is suspected to be compromised. Because this control does not take effect server-side, a session that a user believes to have been terminated can still be used.
**Preconditions**
Exploitation of this issue requires the following conditions:
1. Rancher is configured with an authentication provider that issues external session tokens (for example, OIDC-based providers such as Generic OIDC, Keycloak, or Azure AD). 2. The attacker has already obtained a valid session token belonging to the victim through a separate means outside this flaw (for example, client-side compromise, or leakage through an intermediary proxy, cache, or log). 3. The victim subsequently logs out, expecting the session to be revoked.
An attacker who meets these prerequisites retains authenticated access with the victim's identity and permissions, including administrative privileges where applicable, for the remaining lifetime of the token, despite the victim's logout.
Deployments that do not use public API session tokens are not affected; legacy Rancher API tokens are revoked correctly on logout.
### Patches
The fix corrects the internal routing of the session token identifier during logout. The logout handler now passes the fully qualified token identifier to the token deletion logic, so public API session tokens are deleted from the correct backing store instead of being silently treated as legacy tokens. The deletion path also logs cases where the requested token is not found, so that misrouted deletions are no longer invisible.
Unit test coverage was added for the public API session token logout path, which was previously exercised only for legacy tokens.
This change is not a breaking change and requires no user action beyond upgrading. Sessions issued before the upgrade are revoked normally once the patched version is running.
Rancher v2.15.2 includes the fix for this issue.
### Workarounds
There is no complete workaround other than upgrading to a patched version.
If organizations are unable to upgrade immediately, some partial mitigations are:
- Reduce the session token time-to-live and idle timeout settings in Rancher so that a session that is not revoked at logout expires sooner. - Administrators can delete the affected user's active session tokens directly (for example, by removing the user's tokens through the Rancher API or by disabling the user account) when immediate revocation is required. - Follow standard session-protection practices — enforce TLS end to end, avoid logging or caching authorization headers at intermediary proxies, and restrict the use of untrusted browser extensions on workstations used to administer Rancher — to reduce the likelihood of a session token being captured in the first place.
### References
- [rancher/rancher#57294](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/pull/57294) — fix deletion misrouting, plus unit tests - [rancher/rancher#57293](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/pull/57293) — fix deletion misrouting, plus unit tests (release/v2.15)
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
- Reach out to the [SUSE Rancher Security team](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/policy) for security related inquiries. - Open an issue in the [Rancher](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/new/choose) repository. - Verify our [support matrix](https://www.suse.com/suse-rancher/support-matrix/all-supported-versions/) and [product support life cycle](https://www.suse.com/lifecycle/).

item.title: [MEDIUM] rancher/rancher — Account takeover via principal rebind in Rancher User updates (CVE-2026-71403)
item.description:
CVE-2026-71403 · CVSS 6.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N) · CWE-284, CWE-639
Affected: - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.15.0, <2.15.1 (patched: 2.15.1) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.5 (patched: 2.14.5) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.9 (patched: 2.13.9)
---
### Impact
A security vulnerability exists where the Norman user store `Update` handler (`pkg/auth/api/user/user_store.go`) permits modifications to identity fields (`username`, `principalIds`, and `displayName`) on existing `User` custom resources without enforcing immutability. Although the `Create` path rejects duplicate usernames, the `Update` path lacks an equivalent validation check and accepts arbitrary new principal identifiers.
A caller with `update` permissions on `users.management.cattle.io` can modify the `principalIds` field on any `User` custom resource (CR) to inject an external identity provider principal. When that principal authenticates through a matching external provider (such as LDAP, OIDC, SAML, or Active Directory), the Rancher principal-to-user resolver binds the session to the modified `User` CR instead of provisioning a new user. This behavior transfers all existing role bindings on that `User` CR (`GlobalRoleBindings`, `ClusterRoleTemplateBindings`, and `ProjectRoleTemplateBindings`) to the external identity, enabling account takeover.
An attacker can also create a denial-of-service condition by modifying a target user's `principalIds` to a value that the identity provider never emits. During subsequent external authentication, the user is assigned a new, unbound account, leaving their original role bindings inaccessible.
This issue uses the same identity-rebind primitive previously addressed on the `Create` path in CVE-2024-58260 / GHSA-q82v-h4rq-5c86; that fix did not cover the `Update` path.
#### Preconditions
Exploitation of this security vulnerability requires the following conditions:
- The attacker holds `update` permissions on `users.management.cattle.io`. Standard authenticated users do not possess this verb by default. It applies to administrators, holders of a custom `GlobalRole` granting `users:update`, and (on Rancher 2.10.x release lines only) the deprecated `restricted-admin` role. Authenticated users without this grant receive an HTTP 403 error and cannot reach this code path. - An external authentication provider is configured, and the targeted user subsequently logs in using that provider.
> [!NOTE] > High privilege requirements (`PR:H`) and required user interaction (`UI:R`) are reflected in the CVSS score. Scope is assessed as Unchanged (`S:U`) because cross-boundary execution into downstream clusters was not demonstrated end-to-end.
### Patches
The fix makes the `principalIds` field of a `User` resource immutable after creation, closing the identity-rebind primitive at both layers capable of writing to it:
- **Norman `/v3/users` endpoint:** The user store `Update` handler discards submitted changes to `principalIds` and `username` before the update reaches the Kubernetes API server, preventing values from being persisted. Requests still return `HTTP 200` because fields are dropped silently without an error or warning; clients verifying the outcome must re-read the resource. - **Admission webhook (`rancher-webhook`):** The `users` validator rejects updates modifying `principalIds`, returning `field is immutable`. This protects callers accessing the resource through the Kubernetes API or extension API that bypass Norman handlers. The `manage-users` verb does not exempt callers from this check.
Full protection requires both components: the Rancher manager fix alone does not protect the direct Kubernetes API path, so operators must also deploy the corresponding `rancher-webhook` version.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases `v2.15.1`, `v2.14.5`, and `v2.13.9`.
### Workarounds
No workaround exists other than upgrading to a patched version. Organizations unable to upgrade immediately can reduce exposure by auditing all custom `GlobalRole` resources and remove `update` permissions on `users.management.cattle.io` from non-administrative roles.
### References
- [rancher/rancher#56619](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/pull/56619) — User store immutability fix - [rancher/webhook#1773](https://github.com/rancher/webhook/pull/1773) — Admission webhook immutability enforcement - Related: [CVE-2024-58260 (GHSA-q82v-h4rq-5c86)](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/advisories/GHSA-q82v-h4rq-5c86)
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
- Reach out to the [SUSE Rancher Security team](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/policy) for security related inquiries. - Open an issue in the [Rancher](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/new/choose) repository. - Verify our [support matrix](https://www.suse.com/suse-rancher/support-matrix/all-supported-versions/) and [product support life cycle](https://www.suse.com/lifecycle/).

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/rancher — Unauthorized ClusterRole overwrite via GlobalRole cr-name annotation (CVE-2026-71404)
item.description:
CVE-2026-71404 · CVSS 8.7 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:N/I:H/A:H) · CWE-269, CWE-284, CWE-668
Affected: - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.15.0, <2.15.1 (patched: 2.15.1) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.5 (patched: 2.14.5) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.9 (patched: 2.13.9)
---
### Impact
A security vulnerability exists in Rancher's management-plane GlobalRole controller (`pkg/controllers/management/auth/globalroles/globalrole_handler.go`). The controller derives the name of the backing Kubernetes `ClusterRole` from a user-settable annotation (`authz.management.cattle.io/cr-name`) on a `GlobalRole`. When a `ClusterRole` of that name already exists, the controller overwrites its `.Rules` with the GlobalRole's rules without verifying that the ClusterRole is owned by that GlobalRole.
A user with delegated `create` or `update` permissions for `GlobalRole` resources (`management.cattle.io/globalroles`) on the local management cluster (a non-administrator tier that Rancher supports) can create a `GlobalRole` whose `cr-name` annotation names an arbitrary existing `ClusterRole` (for example the builtin `cluster-admin`) and whose rules are empty. The controller then replaces that ClusterRole's rules with the empty set, stripping the permissions of every principal bound to it, including legitimate Rancher administrators. This results in a cluster-wide RBAC lockout and denial of service on the local management cluster. Because the update path adds no owner-reference, deleting the malicious GlobalRole does not restore the affected ClusterRole and the damage persists until manually repaired.
The webhook escalation check that contains delegated GlobalRole managers only validates the GlobalRole's rule contents against the caller's own permissions and never inspects the `cr-name` annotation, allowing empty rules to pass.
> [!NOTE] > The impact is limited to denial of service (DoS). This issue affects built-in and other non-GlobalRole-owned ClusterRoles that have explicit (non-aggregated) rules. The Kubernetes aggregation controller restores aggregated ClusterRoles such as `admin`, `edit`, and `view`. Exploitation requires an attacker to already hold delegated GlobalRole create or update privileges on the local cluster and does not grant privilege escalation. This is a distinct bypass of the mitigation introduced for GHSA-jwvr / CVE-2021-36784.
### Patches
The fix updates the GlobalRole controller to no longer fetch the `ClusterRole` name from this annotation. Instead, it calculates the name internally and ensures the `ClusterRole` exists with the correct rules. This prevents users from forcing a specific `ClusterRole` name. The system maintains the annotation as a human-readable reference to identify the `ClusterRole` used, but changing the annotation does not affect reconciliation.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases `v2.15.1`, `v2.14.5`, and `v2.13.9`.
### Workarounds
No workaround exists other than upgrading to a patched version. Organizations unable to upgrade immediately can reduce exposure by following these partial mitigations:
- **Restrict permissions:** Audit and limit `create` or `update` permissions on `management.cattle.io/globalroles` to trusted administrators only. - **Audit annotations:** Review `GlobalRole` custom resources for unexpected `authz.management.cattle.io/cr-name` annotations that name `ClusterRole` resources they do not own.
### References
- [GHSA-jwvr / CVE-2021-36784](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/advisories/GHSA-jwvr-vv7p-gpwq) - [rancher/rancher #56593](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/pull/56593) - Removes annotation-based logic for determining cluster role and cluster role binding names in GlobalRoles and GlobalRoleBindings
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
- Reach out to the [SUSE Rancher Security team](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/policy) for security related inquiries. - Open an issue in the [Rancher](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/new/choose) repository. - Verify our [support matrix](https://www.suse.com/suse-rancher/support-matrix/all-supported-versions/) and [product support life cycle](https://www.suse.com/lifecycle/).

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/rancher — Cross-cluster Project Secret disclosure via namespace project ID spoofing in Rancher (CVE-2026-75033)
item.description:
CVE-2026-75033 · CVSS 7.7 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N) · CWE-610, CWE-863
Affected: - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.15.0, <2.15.1 (patched: 2.15.1) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.5 (patched: 2.14.5) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.9 (patched: 2.13.9) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.12.0, <2.12.13 (patched: 2.12.13)
---
### Impact A security vulnerability exists in the Rancher project-scoped `secretsController` (`pkg/controllers/managementuser/secret/`). Project Secrets propagate to a namespace based only on the value of the namespace's `field.cattle.io/projectId` annotation, without validating that the referenced project belongs to the same downstream cluster as the namespace..
A separate instance of the controller runs for each downstream cluster managed by a Rancher instance. Because the namespace handler does not verify that the project referenced by the `projectId` annotation resides in the same cluster, an attacker can create a namespace in a cluster they control with a `projectId` annotation matching a project in a different cluster. The controller then propagates the Project Secrets from that target cluster's project into the attacker-controlled namespace, disclosing secrets (including credentials, API keys, and TLS certificates) across the cluster trust boundary.
#### Preconditions
Exploitation of this security vulnerability requires the following conditions:
- The attacker must be an authenticated Rancher user with permissions to create namespaces (such as Cluster Owner) on at least one downstream cluster managed by the same Rancher instance. - The attacker must know or guess the target project ID (format `c-xxxxx:p-yyyyy`), which references a project containing Project Secrets in a cluster the attacker is not authorized to access. - No interaction from any other user is required.
> [!NOTE] > This affects Rancher deployments managing more than one cluster. The issue is confirmed in Rancher 2.14.3.
### Patches The fix adds cluster-scoping validation to project-scoped secret handling. When processing a namespace's `field.cattle.io/projectId` annotation, the controller verifies that the cluster component of the project ID matches the cluster where the namespace resides. If the referenced project belongs to a different cluster, secret propagation is skipped and the cross-cluster `projectId` is rejected on namespace creation and update.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases 2.15.1, 2.14.5, 2.13.9, and 2.12.13.
### Workarounds No workaround exists other than upgrading to a patched version. Organizations unable to upgrade immediately can reduce exposure by auditing and restricting namespace creation permissions on downstream clusters, and by auditing existing namespaces for `field.cattle.io/projectId` annotations that reference cross-cluster projects.
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
- Reach out to the [SUSE Rancher Security team](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/policy) for security related inquiries. - Open an issue in the [Rancher](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/new/choose) repository. - Verify our [support matrix](https://www.suse.com/suse-rancher/support-matrix/all-supported-versions/) and [product support life cycle](https://www.suse.com/lifecycle/).

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/rancher — Cross-replica SAML assertion replay in Rancher HA deployments (CVE-2026-75034)
item.description:
CVE-2026-75034 · CVSS 7.4 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N) · CWE-294
Affected: - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.15.0, <2.15.1 (patched: 2.15.1) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.5 (patched: 2.14.5) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.9 (patched: 2.13.9) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.12.0, <2.12.13 - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.11.0, <2.11.17
---
### Impact A security vulnerability exists in the Rancher Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) handler when Rancher is deployed in high-availability (HA) mode with multiple replicas.
The replay protection introduced by the fix for [CVE-2026-44946](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/advisories/GHSA-c5jm-xcmq-9j95) relies on instance-level tracking of SAML assertion IDs. In high-availability (HA) deployments with multiple replicas, instances do not share this tracking mechanism. Consequently, other replicas do not recognize an assertion that one replica has already consumed. When a request routes to a different pod, that replica accepts the assertion again. This creates a window where other instances in the deployment can accept captured assertions, potentially establishing additional authenticated sessions.
This issue affects all SAML-based authentication providers that Rancher supports (including Okta, Ping, AD FS, Keycloak, and Shibboleth) because they all share the same ACS handler.
#### Preconditions
Exploitation of this security vulnerability requires the following conditions:
- Rancher is configured to use a SAML-based authentication provider. - Rancher is deployed in HA mode with two or more replicas behind a load balancer. Single-replica deployments remain unaffected because the in-memory cache is authoritative for all requests. - The attacker can obtain a valid, signed SAML assertion issued during a victim's authentication flow (for example, through network interception, IdP log exposure, or by leveraging another vulnerability such as XSS), along with the associated pre-authentication SAML state. - The assertion is replayed while it is still within its validity window (`NotBefore` / `NotOnOrAfter`), which is typically short (a few minutes).
### Patches The fix replaces the per-process, in-memory assertion ID cache with a shared, cluster-wide store so that all replicas track consumed assertion IDs consistently. Once any replica records an assertion ID, the system rejects subsequent submissions of that same assertion, regardless of which pod handles the request. To limit storage growth, entries expire based on the assertion's validity window.
The system continues to enforce strict validation of the SAML assertion's `NotBefore` and `NotOnOrAfter` time conditions (introduced with the fix for CVE-2026-44946), limiting the validity window of captured assertions.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases v2.15.1, v2.14.5, and v2.13.9.
### Workarounds No workaround exists other than upgrading to a patched version. Organizations unable to upgrade immediately can reduce exposure by following these partial mitigations:
- **Run a single replica:** Running Rancher with a single replica eliminates the cross-pod replay window, but compromises high availability. SUSE does not recommend this configuration for production environments. - **Reduce SAML validity windows:** Reducing the SAML assertion validity window at the identity provider (IdP) level limits the timeframe in which an attacker can replay a captured assertion. - **Restrict network access:** Restricting network access to the Rancher SAML Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) endpoint and enforcing TLS between clients and Rancher reduces the likelihood of intercepting traffic, but does not eliminate the vulnerability.
### References - [rancher/rancher #56778](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/pull/56778) — Adds persistent in-cluster storage for SAML assertion IDs to replace the in-memory store - Related: [CVE-2026-44946 (GHSA-c5jm-xcmq-9j95)](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/advisories/GHSA-c5jm-xcmq-9j95)
### For more information
If you have any questions or comments about this advisory:
- Reach out to the [SUSE Rancher Security team](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/policy) for security related inquiries. - Open an issue in the [Rancher](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/new/choose) repository. - Verify our [support matrix](https://www.suse.com/suse-rancher/support-matrix/all-supported-versions/) and [product support life cycle](https://www.suse.com/lifecycle/).

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/rancher — Cross-user token disclosure via label-selector bypass in Rancher’s ext Token API (CVE-2026-75035)
item.description:
CVE-2026-75035 · CVSS 7.1 (CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N) · CWE-200, CWE-639, CWE-863
Affected: - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.15.0, <2.15.1 (patched: 2.15.1) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.5 (patched: 2.14.5) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.9 (patched: 2.13.9) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.12.0, <2.12.13
---
### Impact A security vulnerability exists in the imperative ext Token API (`ext.cattle.io/v1`, resource `tokens`, backed by Secrets in the `cattle-tokens` namespace) in `pkg/ext/stores/tokens`. The store enforces per-user scoping of these tokens internally rather than through role-based access control (RBAC). Because default built-in **User** and **User Base** global roles grant every authenticated user self-service verbs (such as `get`, `list`, and `watch`) on `tokens`, the store's list/watch scoping logic is the only control limiting callers to their own tokens.
When a non-administrative caller supplies a label selector specifying a different user (`cattle.io/user-id=<other-user>`), the scoping logic fails. Instead of returning an empty result, the store drops its internal owner filter and executes the backing Secret list/watch request using only the caller-supplied selector, without performing a subsequent ownership check.
As a result, any authenticated Rancher user can list and watch any other user's tokens across the entire Rancher instance. Each disclosed token object exposes metadata, including owner user ID, principal or login name, authentication provider, cluster scope, TTL, kind, and description. Additionally, a companion defect causes read responses to include `status.hash`, which contains the stored salted hash of the bearer token (sensitive server-side authentication material).
Single-object read, update, and delete operations remain owner-checked and are unaffected. Mass deletion through `DeleteCollection` shares the scoping defect but requires the `deletecollection` verb, which default user roles do not possess (standard authenticated users cannot reach this operation).
> [!NOTE] > Rancher `v2.11` and earlier do not include the ext token store and are **not** affected. The fix also ships in the `v2.16.0` development line.
#### Preconditions
Exploitation of this security vulnerability requires the following conditions:
- The target Rancher deployment runs version 2.12.0 or later, which includes the ext token store (see the affected versions table). - The attacker holds a standard authenticated Rancher account assigned default **User** or **User Base** global roles (the out-of-the-box baseline). Administrative privileges are not required.
> [!NOTE] > Exploitation does not require non-default configurations or feature flags. The vulnerability affects out-of-the-box default configurations for all authenticated users.
### Patches The fix hardens per-user `list`, `watch`, and `deletecollection` scoping in the store, preventing non-administrative callers from widening scope using caller-supplied selectors. The store now unconditionally appends the requesting user's owner requirement (`cattle.io/user-id=<self>`) to the caller's selector using an AND operation. As a result, any selector specifying a different user contains conflicting equality requirements on the owner label, making the query unsatisfiable and returning no results. Administrative full-access workflows remain unchanged.
In addition, the store now parses selectors with full label-selector syntax, resolving a separate issue where set-based, inequality, and existence selectors returned HTTP 500 errors.
The store also strips the stored token hash (`status.hash`) from all read responses (`get`, `list`, `watch`, and responses to `update`), mirroring behavior on the create path. The hash remains solely on the backing Secret and the internal accessor required to preserve it across updates, maintaining standard token authentication functionality.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases v2.15.1, v2.14.5, and v2.13.9.
### Workarounds No workaround exists other than upgrading to a patched version. For organizations unable to upgrade, operators can detect attempted exploitation in audit logs by monitoring `list` and `watch` requests to `ext.cattle.io/v1` `tokens`. Any request from a non-administrative user where `labelSelector` contains `cattle.io/user-id=<value>` with a value that does not match the requesting user's ID is anomalous.

item.title: [CRITICAL] rancher/rancher — Privilege escalation in Rancher's local cluster due to cross-cluster impersonation (confused-deputy problem) (CVE-2026-44945)
item.description:
CVE-2026-44945 · CVSS 9.1 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H) · CWE-441
Affected: - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.2 (patched: 2.14.4) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.8 (patched: 2.13.8) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.12.0, <2.12.12 (patched: 2.12.12) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.11.0, <2.11.16 (patched: 2.11.16)
---
### Impact
A privilege escalation vulnerability exists in Rancher's impersonation middleware (`pkg/auth/requests/impersonate.go`). An authenticated Rancher user with the default `user` global role can gain full administrative access to the Rancher control plane and transitively to all downstream clusters it manages.
Rancher's `ImpersonationMiddleware` authorizes impersonation requests by running a Kubernetes `SubjectAccessReview` (SAR) against the cluster whose ID is parsed from the request URL path. However, the subsequent request is served by Rancher's management API (`managementAPI`), which operates against the **local** Rancher management cluster via the `scaledContext` service account. The `Impersonate-User`, `Impersonate-Group`, and `Impersonate-Extra-*` headers written by the middleware are forwarded verbatim by the Norman proxy store to that local Kubernetes API. Because the SAR authorization check and the actual request execution target are in different clusters, an attacker who controls RBAC on any downstream cluster can authorize themselves to impersonate privileged identities-including `system:masters` against the local Rancher cluster.
Successful exploitation allows the attacker to read all secrets stored by Rancher (kubeconfigs, authentication-provider credentials, LDAP bind passwords, OIDC client secrets, SAML signing keys), create or modify `GlobalRoleBindings`, and take full administrative control of all clusters managed by the affected Rancher instance.
**Note:** Exploitation requires an authenticated Rancher session and RBAC control on at least one downstream cluster registered with Rancher. Any user with the default `user` global role can import their own cluster; an attacker-controlled throwaway cluster (e.g., local k3d, kind, or minikube) is sufficient. No pre-existing access to production clusters, no elevated Rancher role, and no victim interaction is required.
### Patches
The vulnerability was fixed by ensuring that SAR-based impersonation permission checks are always evaluated against the **local** Rancher management cluster rather than a cluster derived from the URL path. Specifically:
- `pkg/auth/requests/sar/sar.go`: `NewSubjectAccessReview` now accepts a fixed `authorizationv1.SubjectAccessReviewInterface` client constructed from the local cluster's `scaledContext`, replacing the per-request `SubjectAccessReviewClientGetter` that previously resolved the SAR target cluster from the URL path. - `pkg/auth/requests/sar/middleware.go`: The SAR middleware now reads the authenticated user identity from the request context (set by the authentication layer) instead of trusting `Impersonate-User` / `Impersonate-Group` HTTP headers directly.
The fix is included in Rancher `v2.14.4`, `v2.13.8`, `v2.12.12` and `v2.11.16`.
### Workarounds
There is no complete workaround that eliminates the vulnerability without upgrading to a patched version. Organizations that cannot upgrade immediately may reduce exposure by auditing and restricting which users are permitted to register downstream clusters in Rancher. By default, any user with the `user` global role can import clusters; removing or restricting this permission limits the attack surface but does not fully remediate the vulnerability.
### References
- PR [rancher/rancher#55983](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/pull/55983)

This vulnerability was discovered and reported by [@BenTheCyberOne](https://github.com/BenTheCyberOne).

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/rancher — Rancher Audit-Log Middleware Unauthenticated Memory Exhaustion Denial of Service (CVE-2026-59675)
item.description:
CVE-2026-59675 · CVSS 7.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H) · CWE-770
Affected: - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.4 (patched: 2.14.4) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.8 (patched: 2.13.8) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.12.0, <2.12.12 (patched: 2.12.12)
---
### Impact
A denial of service vulnerability exists in Rancher's API audit-log middleware (`pkg/auth/audit`). When API audit logging is enabled, the middleware reads the entire HTTP request body into memory without enforcing a size limit on login endpoints. Because the audit middleware is positioned earlier in the handler chain than Rancher's `APIBodyLimitingHandler`, the body-size cap (default 1 MiB) is bypassed for requests that pass through the audit `copyReqBody` path. An unauthenticated attacker can send arbitrarily large request bodies to the public login endpoints, causing the Rancher Manager server process to allocate memory proportional to the supplied body size. With just a few concurrent connections, this can exhaust available memory and terminate the Rancher Manager plane process, making the Rancher API and UI unavailable and interrupting management of all downstream clusters.
Please consult the associated [MITRE ATT&CK - Technique - Endpoint Denial of Service](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1499/) for further information about this category of attack.
**Preconditions**
For this vulnerability to be exploitable, the following must apply:
1. API audit logging is enabled on the Rancher server (`--enable-audit-log` / `AUDIT_LOG_ENABLED=true`). This is **not enabled by default**; however, it is a commonly recommended configuration in production and compliance-driven environments.
2. The attacker has network access to the Rancher management HTTPS endpoint. No credentials, tokens, or prior account access are required.
**Note:** Rancher deployments with API audit logging disabled are **not** affected by this vulnerability.
### Patches
The fix restricts the response body read in the audit middleware's `copyReqBody` function (`pkg/auth/audit/log.go`) for login endpoints. The previously unbounded `io.ReadAll(req.Body)` call is replaced with a read capped at the limit configured for Rancher's `APIBodyLimitingHandler`, where the `APIBodyLimit` default setting is 1 MiB. Request bodies that exceed this limit are truncated in the audit log rather than fully buffered, preventing runaway memory allocation.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases `v2.14.4`, `v2.13.8`, and `v2.12.12`.
### Workarounds
No workaround available.
### Credits
This vulnerability was discovered and reported by `securityraven@proton.me`.

item.title: [MEDIUM] rancher/rancher — Cluster Existence Oracle via Unauthenticated Import Endpoint (CVE-2026-55998)
item.description:
CVE-2026-55998 · CVSS 5.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N) · CWE-204
Affected: - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.4 (patched: 2.14.4) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.8 (patched: 2.13.8) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.12.0, <2.12.12 (patched: 2.12.12) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.11.0, <2.11.16 (patched: 2.11.16)
---
### Impact
A vulnerability in Rancher's unauthenticated cluster import endpoint allows an external attacker to enumerate valid cluster IDs and determine whether a cluster is configured with private registry secrets.
The endpoint `/v3/import/{token}_{clusterId}.yaml` retrieves the cluster object before validating the token. When a valid cluster ID references a cluster that has private registry secrets configured, a nil pointer dereference in `pkg/systemtemplate/private_registry.go` causes the request to return `HTTP 502 Bad Gateway`. For cluster IDs that do not exist, the endpoint returns `HTTP 200`. This observable difference in response codes constitutes a reliable enumeration oracle.
An unauthenticated attacker with network access to the Rancher API can exploit this behavior to:
- Enumerate valid Rancher cluster IDs - Identify which clusters are configured with private registry secrets - Fingerprint the infrastructure for use in follow-on attacks
**Preconditions**
For the `HTTP 502` side-channel to be triggered, the targeted cluster must have private registry secrets configured. Clusters without private registry secrets do not exhibit the distinguishable error response. However, a non-existent cluster ID always returns `HTTP 200`, making it possible to enumerate existing clusters regardless of their private registry configuration. The endpoint is publicly accessible and requires no authentication.
### Patches
The fix validates the token before loading the cluster object, so an invalid or unauthenticated request cannot reach the cluster-lookup and private-registry code paths. With the patch applied, invalid requests receive a uniform response regardless of cluster existence or configuration.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases `v2.14.4`, `v2.13.8`, `v2.12.12`, and `v2.11.16`.
### Workarounds
If upgrading to a patched version is not immediately possible, operators can reduce exposure by restricting network access to the Rancher API (`/v3/import/`) to trusted networks using a firewall, reverse proxy, or network policy, so that unauthenticated requests from untrusted sources cannot reach the endpoint.
There is no configuration change within Rancher that fully mitigates this issue without upgrading.
### Credits
This vulnerability was discovered and reported by Michael Wollner ([`@ibonok`](https://github.com/ibonok)) from Deutsche Telekom AG.

item.title: [MEDIUM] rancher/rancher — Unauthenticated Denial-of-Service via TLS SAN Stuffing in Rancher and cattle-cluster-agent (CVE-2026-55996)
item.description:
CVE-2026-55996 · CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:L)
Affected: - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.4 (patched: 2.14.4) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.8 (patched: 2.13.8) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.12.0, <2.12.12 (patched: 2.12.12) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.11.0, <2.11.16 (patched: 2.11.16)
---
### Impact
A denial-of-service vulnerability was identified in multiple TLS listeners in Rancher. Both the `cattle-cluster-agent` component running in downstream clusters and the Rancher server itself use the `dynamiclistener` library to serve TLS traffic. Without an effective CN filter configured, `dynamiclistener` automatically appended to each serving certificate any hostname presented via Server Name Indication (SNI) in incoming TLS requests.
Two listeners were affected:
- **`cattle-cluster-agent` port 443 (`serving-cert`)** in downstream clusters: no CN filter, reachable via direct pod-IP access only. - **Rancher server port 444 (`tls-rancher-internal`)** on the upstream cluster: no CN filter, reachable via the `rancher-internal` ClusterIP Service.
An unauthenticated attacker with network access within the affected cluster could send a large number of TLS requests with distinct hostnames, causing the serving certificate to accumulate an unbounded number of Subject Alternative Names (SANs). Eventually, the certificate grows large enough that TLS handshakes fail with an excessive message size error, causing a denial of service on the affected listeners.
**Note:** Exploitation requires at least minimal privileges within the Kubernetes cluster — for example, the ability to run or exec into a pod — in order to reach the cluster-internal network. Port 443 on `cattle-cluster-agent` is not exposed via a Kubernetes Service and requires direct pod-IP access. The Rancher server's internal port 444 is reachable via the `rancher-internal` ClusterIP Service from within the upstream cluster.
### Patches
The fix addresses two listeners:
- **`cattle-cluster-agent` port 443 (`serving-cert`):** When running in embedded MCM agent mode (`features.MCMAgent`), the `filterCN` callback now returns nil, rejecting all dynamically presented SNI hostnames. The serving certificate is restricted to its pre-configured static Subject Alternative Names only, preventing any attacker-supplied hostname from being appended.
- **Upstream Rancher port 444 (`tls-rancher-internal`):** A pod-IP-tracking filter (`FilterCN`) was added together with `FilterExisting: true` and a maximum SAN count of 30. The filter retains only IP entries corresponding to currently-running Rancher pods; stale pod IPs from previous rollouts and any attacker-injected IPs are pruned on the next certificate operation.
The fix requires an update to the `rancher/dynamiclistener` dependency.
The following Rancher versions contain the fix: `v2.11.16`, `v2.12.12`, `v2.13.8`, and `v2.14.4`.
### Workarounds
There is no complete workaround for users who cannot upgrade. As a partial mitigation, restrict access to the affected cluster-internal endpoints using Kubernetes `NetworkPolicy` resources to ensure only trusted workloads can reach:
- The `cattle-cluster-agent` pod IP on port 443 in downstream clusters - The `rancher-internal` ClusterIP Service on port 444 on the upstream cluster
This reduces the attack surface but does not eliminate the vulnerability.
### References
- [GHSA-p45j-vfv5-wprq](https://github.com/rancher/rke2/security/advisories/GHSA-p45j-vfv5-wprq) — Similar TLS SAN stuffing issue in RKE2 via `dynamiclistener`

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/rancher — Long-lived Rancher registration token exposed in plaintext (CVE-2026-55997)
item.description:
CVE-2026-55997 · CVSS 8.8 (CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H) · CWE-312, CWE-522, CWE-732
Affected: - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.4 (patched: 2.14.4) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.8 (patched: 2.13.8)
---
### Impact
Rancher issues long-lived registration tokens to authenticate nodes and agents joining a downstream cluster. These tokens were stored and exposed in plaintext with no expiration, so a malicious user could obtain one either through the Rancher API, etcd, stored automation, or direct file access on a node, and could use it at any time to register a rogue node into the cluster.
Two surfaces exposed this same class of token:
- **`ClusterRegistrationToken` (CRT) objects:** The token was stored in the plaintext `status.Token` field of the CRD and returned to cluster administrators via the Rancher API. Because it never expired, it remained usable indefinitely once obtained, including from copied registration commands left in shell history, CI/CD pipelines, or infrastructure-as-code. - **v2prov (RKE2/K3s) install script:** During provisioning, the system agent install script (`/usr/local/custom_script/install.sh`) is written to each downstream node with world-readable permissions (`0644`), embedding the `CATTLE_TOKEN` bootstrap credential, server URL, and CA checksum. Any local user or process on the node, even without any Rancher API access, could read it directly.
In both cases, an attacker who obtains the token can register a node with controlplane or etcd roles, gaining full administrative control of the affected downstream cluster (PKI, etcd data, secrets, workloads).
Rancher's audit logging already redacts token fields via the `sensitiveBodyFields` policy (`pkg/auth/audit/`); this advisory addresses the underlying plaintext storage and file-permission gaps, which exist independently of audit logging.
**Preconditions**
- The attacker must obtain a valid registration token, via cluster-admin-level Rancher API access, etcd, stored/copied registration commands, or for v2prov nodes local (non-root) code execution on a provisioned node.
### Patches
1. **Secret-based token storage:** CRT tokens are now stored in Kubernetes Secrets (`crt-token-<crt-name>`) in the cluster's namespace instead of the CRD's `status.Token` field. A one-time migration moves existing tokens into Secrets at startup; CRT status fields thereafter use a `{token}` placeholder instead of the real credential. 2. **API compatibility shims:** Norman and Steve API shims substitute the real token from the Secret when CRTs are requested through the Rancher API. Direct `kubectl` access returns the `{token}` placeholder; obtaining the real value requires RBAC access to the Secret. 3. **Opt-in TTL-based token rotation:** The `crt-token-ttl-rotation` feature flag enables automatic CRT token expiration and rotation, configurable via `CRTDefaultTTL`/`CRTDefaultGracePeriod` settings or per-CRT overrides. On expiry, a new token is generated; both old and new tokens remain valid during the grace period giving agents time to pick up the new credential. Rotation is paired with new detection logic in `clusterDeploy` that recognizes when a cluster's token has changed and automatically redeploys the cluster agent with the new credential. Token rotation alone would otherwise never reach a running agent. The feature flag is opt-in for 2.13 and 2.14, and enabled by default starting in 2.15. 4. **RBAC for Secret access:** A new `crt-token-reader` Role is created per cluster namespace; with `AggregatedRoleTemplates` enabled, the CRTB controller automatically creates matching RoleBindings. 5. **Install script permission hardening:** Script permissions changed from `0644` to `0600`, preventing non-privileged local users from reading it directly. 6. **Bootstrap token TTL invalidation (2.15 only, not backported):** System agent bootstrap tokens now automatically expire with a short TTL (default 30s) after first contact with `v3/connect/agent`, and a long TTL (default 30m from creation) regardless of use. This applies only to the v2prov bootstrap token, not CRTs or upgrade tokens.
The following versions of Rancher contain the fix: `v2.14.4` and `v2.13.8`.
### Workarounds
There is no complete workaround; the following reduce risk while patching is pending:
- **Restrict install script permissions manually:** `chmod 0600 /usr/local/custom_script/install.sh` on each provisioned node. Containers with a host path mount to `/usr/local` can still read the file as root even after this change. - **Limit local access on downstream nodes:** Avoid granting untrusted workloads host path access, especially to `/usr/local`. - **Limit access to token exposure surfaces:** Restrict access to etcd backups, infrastructure-as-code repositories, CI/CD configuration, and shell history where registration commands may have been copied or stored. - **Rotate compromised tokens:** If a specific `system` CRT is known or suspected to be compromised, delete it to force generation of a new token, patch the cluster agent's credential with the new token, then redeploy the agent to pick it up. New connection attempts using the old token are rejected as soon as the token is rotated, however, the agent's existing tunnel connection is not immediately dropped, so this must be paired with an explicit credential patch, a plain agent restart alone will not fetch the new token. This is a manual, per-cluster, disruptive procedure and is not a practical way to rotate tokens broadly across many clusters.
### For more information

- Reach out to the [SUSE Rancher Security team](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/security/policy) for security related inquiries. - Open an issue in the [Rancher](https://github.com/rancher/rancher/issues/new/choose) repository. - Verify our [support matrix](https://www.suse.com/suse-rancher/support-matrix/all-supported-versions/) and [product support life cycle](https://www.suse.com/lifecycle/).

item.title: [MEDIUM] rancher/rancher — Stale PSA ClusterRoleBinding Persists After RoleTemplate Downgrade in Rancher (CVE-2026-44947)
item.description:
CVE-2026-44947 · CVSS 4.9 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N) · CWE-281
Affected: - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.3 (patched: 2.14.3) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.7 (patched: 2.13.7)
---
### Impact
A vulnerability in the legacy Project Role Template Binding (PRTB) reconciler in Rancher allows users to retain unauthorized Pod Security Admission (PSA) permissions after an administrator removes those permissions from a RoleTemplate.
When the `aggregated-roletemplates` feature is disabled (the default configuration), removing the `updatepsa` permission from a RoleTemplate does not trigger cleanup of the associated PSA ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding. As a result, the affected user retains the ability to modify PSA enforcement levels across project namespaces even after explicit revocation. Stale permissions persist indefinitely, surviving both RoleTemplate downgrades and subsequent deletion of the PRTB.
**Preconditions**
For this vulnerability to be exploitable, all of the following must apply:
1. The Rancher installation uses the legacy PRTB reconciler, i.e., the `aggregated-roletemplates` feature flag is disabled (this is the default behavior). 2. An administrator has previously created a RoleTemplate that grants the `updatepsa` permission (`verb: updatepsa, resource: project, apiGroup: management.cattle.io`) and assigned it to a user via a PRTB. 3. The administrator subsequently removes the `updatepsa` permission from the RoleTemplate without manually deleting the user's PSA ClusterRoleBinding.
**Notes:**
- The `aggregated-roletemplates` handler (when enabled) performs desired-state reconciliation and is not affected by this issue. - Rancher versions 2.12 and 2.11 are not receiving a patch for this security issue. Please review the workarounds section below for proper mitigations.
### Patches
The legacy PRTB reconciler has been updated to correctly clean up stale PSA ClusterRoles and ClusterRoleBindings when the `updatepsa` permission is removed from a RoleTemplate. The `ensurePSAPermissions()` function in `pkg/controllers/managementuser/rbac/prtb_handler.go` now invokes the cleanup path when the permission is no longer present, ensuring that PSA artifacts are removed during reconciliation.
The following versions of Rancher contain the fix: 2.14.3 and 2.13.7.
### Workarounds
For environments that cannot immediately upgrade, administrators can mitigate the issue by manually identifying and deleting stale PSA ClusterRoles and ClusterRoleBindings after downgrading a RoleTemplate that previously granted `updatepsa`. The ClusterRoles will be of the form `<projectID>-namespaces-psa`. Delete any ClusterRoles with that name and any ClusterRoleBindings that reference the ClusterRoles for RoleTemplates that should no longer have `updatepsa` permissions.
### Credits
This vulnerability was discovered and reported by [bugbunny.ai](https://bugbunny.ai/).

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/rancher — SAML Authentication Replay in Rancher (CVE-2026-44946)
item.description:
CVE-2026-44946 · CVSS 7.4 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N) · CWE-294
Affected: - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.3 (patched: 2.14.3) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.7 (patched: 2.13.7) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.12.0, <2.12.11 (patched: 2.12.11) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.11.0, <2.11.15 (patched: 2.11.15)
---
### Impact A SAML authentication replay vulnerability exists in Rancher's Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) handler. Rancher's SAML login does not enforce one-time use of SAML assertions: the same signed SAML response can be submitted more than once to obtain separate authenticated sessions.
This vulnerability affects all SAML-based authentication providers supported by Rancher, including Okta, Ping, ADFS, Keycloak, and Shibboleth, because they all share the same ACS handler (`pkg/auth/providers/saml/saml_client.go`).
**Preconditions:**
Successful exploitation requires the following conditions: 1. Rancher is configured to use a SAML-based authentication provider. 2. The attacker can obtain a valid, signed SAML response issued during a victim's authentication flow (for example, through network interception, access to logs containing authentication artifacts, or by leveraging another vulnerability such as XSS). 3. The attacker can obtain the victim's corresponding pre-authentication SAML state cookie.
An attacker who meets these prerequisites can replay the captured SAML response together with the associated state cookie to establish a new authenticated Rancher session as the victim. The resulting session inherits all permissions assigned to the victim account, including administrative privileges where applicable, enabling full impersonation of the affected user.
### Patches The fix adds server-side tracking of SAML assertion IDs. When a SAML assertion is processed, its ID is stored in an in-memory cache. The cache entry expires at the assertion's `NotOnOrAfter` time (or after one hour if no expiry is specified). Any subsequent submission of the same assertion ID is rejected.
Additionally, the fix enforces strict validation of the SAML assertion's `NotBefore` and `NotOnOrAfter` time conditions, rejecting assertions that fall outside their validity window.
These changes are applied in the shared ACS handler and therefore protect all SAML providers (Okta, Ping, ADFS, Keycloak, Shibboleth) simultaneously.
Rancher `v2.14.3`, `v2.13.7`, `v2.12.11` and `v2.11.15`, include the fix for this issue.
### Workarounds There is no complete workaround for users who cannot upgrade.
As a partial mitigation, reducing the SAML assertion validity window at the Identity Provider level limits the time window in which a captured assertion can be replayed.
Restricting network access to the Rancher SAML ACS endpoint and enforcing TLS inspection between clients and Rancher reduces the practical feasibility of intercepting SAML traffic, but does not eliminate the vulnerability.

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/rancher — Privilege Escalation from Project Owner to Host (CVE-2026-41052)
item.description:
CVE-2026-41052 · CVSS 8.4 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H)
Affected: - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.2 (patched: 2.14.2) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.6 (patched: 2.13.6) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.12.0, <2.12.10 (patched: 2.12.10)
---
### Impact
A vulnerability has been identified in Rancher Manager that allows users assigned the Project Owner role to modify Pod Security Admission (PSA) labels on namespaces within their projects. Under the default role configuration, an attacker with the following access pattern can exploit this issue: 1. **Cluster Access:** The user is granted Cluster Member access. 2. **Project Ownership:** The user creates or is assigned ownership of a project. 3. **Namespace Creation:** The user creates a namespace within that project. 4. **PSA Modification:** The user modifies the namespace PSA configuration to use the privileged profile. 5. **Privilege Escalation:** The user deploys privileged workloads within the namespace.
As outlined in the [Kubernetes Pod Security Standards](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/) documentation, `privileged` containers disable core Kubernetes security protections, allowing workloads to bypass standard container isolation boundaries. This can result in privilege escalation within the cluster environment.
Potential impacts include: - Deployment of privileged containers - Access to host-level resources - Container breakout - Cluster privilege escalation - Compromise of workloads running on affected nodes
Please refer to the associated MITRE ATT&CK techniques for further information about this category of attack: - [Deploy Container](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1610/) - [Escape to Host](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1611/) - [Exploitation for Privilege Escalation](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068)
Reference: [Kubernetes Pod Security Standards — Privileged Profile](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/security/pod-security-standards/#privileged)
### Patches This vulnerability is resolved by modifying the `project-owner` role to explicitly define the allowed verbs for `projects` resources instead of using the wildcard `(*)` permission.
The updated role configuration removes access to the `updatepsa` verb. This prevents project owners from modifying PSA settings in a manner that could enable privilege escalation.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases `v2.12.10`, `v2.13.6`, and `v2.14.2`.
### Workarounds If upgrading is not immediately possible, administrators should create a custom project role based on the existing Project Owner role, while removing unrestricted wildcard permissions for project resources.
The allowed verbs for projects should be restricted to: “`get`, `update`, `delete`, `patch`, `create`, `list`, `watch`, `deletecollection`” instead of “`*`”.
This prevents access to the `updatepsa` capability that enables the privilege escalation path.

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/rancher — Over-inclusive team membership expansion in GitHub App authentication provider (CVE-2026-41053)
item.description:
CVE-2026-41053 · CVSS 8.8 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H)
Affected: - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.2 (patched: 2.14.2) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.6 (patched: 2.13.6)
---
### Impact A vulnerability has been identified within Rancher Manager in the GitHub App authentication provider. When evaluating permissions, the provider incorrectly expands user team memberships to include all teams within the associated GitHub organization, rather than restricting access to the specific teams to which the user actually belongs.
Specifically, when a user authenticates via the GitHub App provider, Rancher's team membership evaluation logic incorrectly handles cached data. Instead of checking the user-specific list, the evaluation logic iterates over all teams defined within the entire GitHub organization. The authentication provider should consult the correctly cached, per-user membership list to assign the user's specific group permissions. Consequently, any authenticated user who belongs to at least one team in a GitHub organization is mistakenly granted `group principals` for every team within that entire organization during authentication and authorization checks.
This issue allows a malicious user who is a member of a low-privilege team within a GitHub organization to gain unauthorized access to or permissions for any other team in that organization. If those other teams are bound to Rancher login allowlists or RBAC roles (cluster-level, project-level, or global), the attacker can pass access checks that should otherwise fail, inheriting permissions they were never granted.
**Exploitation of this vulnerability requires the following conditions to be met:** - The GitHub App authentication provider must be enabled and configured for the target GitHub organization. - The attacker must possess a valid GitHub account with membership in at least one team within that target organization. - A separate team within the same GitHub organization must be explicitly mapped to Rancher RBAC roles or specified within Rancher's login allowlist (`allowedPrincipalIds`).
Please consult the associated [MITRE ATT&CK - Technique - Valid Accounts](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1078/) for further information about this category of attack.
### Patches This fix corrects the team listing logic to iterate only the teams stored in the per-user membership cache and includes a one-time startup migration that marks all affected User resources for refresh, forcing Rancher to rebuild `group principals` using the now-corrected logic.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases `v2.14.2` and `v2.13.6`.
### Workarounds If upgrading to a patched version immediately is not feasible, users are encouraged to consider these temporary mitigations: - Disable GitHub App authentication provider and switch to an alternative authentication provider (GitHub OAuth). - Remove or restrict team-based `group principals` from allowed principalIds. - Audit and temporarily remove RBAC bindings (`GlobalRoleBindings`, `ClusterRoleTemplateBindings`, `ProjectRoleTemplateBindings`) that reference GitHub App team `principals` until the patch is applied. - Disable provider refresh and clean up inflated group membership for users (manually or by writing a script).
These workarounds reduce the attack surface but do not eliminate the vulnerability. Existing user sessions and cached principals remain inflated until a provider refresh occurs. Upgrading to a patched version is strongly recommended.

item.title: [CRITICAL] rancher/rancher — Command injection through unsanitized YAML parameter in Rancher (CVE-2026-44939)
item.description:
CVE-2026-44939 · CVSS 9.6 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H)
Affected: - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0, <2.14.2 (patched: 2.14.2) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.6 (patched: 2.13.6) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.12.0, <2.12.10 (patched: 2.12.10) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.11.0, <2.11.14 (patched: 2.11.14) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.10.0, <2.10.12 (patched: 2.10.12)
---
### Impact A critical command injection vulnerability has been identified in the Rancher Manager cluster import endpoint `/v3/import/{token}_{clusterId}.yaml` through unsanitized YAML parameters. This endpoint accepts an `authImage` query parameter that is rendered without sanitization into a generated Kubernetes manifest template. By including URL-encoded newlines in the parameter value, an attacker can break out of the `image:` field to inject arbitrary YAML keys and malicious configurations, such as commands to execute malicious containers.
Exploitation of this vulnerability requires the following conditions to be met: - Attackers must obtain a valid cluster registration token (these tokens may be exposed, for example, through documentation, screenshots, or insecure communication channels). - The victim’s cluster operator must execute `kubectl apply` against a maliciously crafted URL.
When a victim applies this compromised manifest using `kubectl apply`, a DaemonSet is deployed with the injected configuration. This DaemonSet: - Runs on all control-plane nodes with `hostNetwork: true` enabled. - Uses the `cattle` service account, which possesses `cluster-admin` privileges. - Mounts `/etc/kubernetes` directly from the host. - Executes attacker-controlled commands via the injected `command:` field.
An attacker who successfully exploits this vulnerability could:
- Achieve full control over downstream Kubernetes clusters. - Execute arbitrary code on control-plane nodes with elevated privileges. - Access sensitive cluster secrets and configurations via the privileged service account. - Disrupt cluster operations by manipulating critical control-plane workloads. - Establish persistent access through the deployed DaemonSet.
**Note:** If you believe that you might have been impacted by this vulnerability, it's highly advised to review your clusters' logs and deployment logs for signs of malicious deployments and to rotate all service accounts and credentials that might have been exposed in such a scenario.
Please refer to the associated [MITRE ATT&CK - Technique - Deploy Container](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1610/) for further information about this category of attack.
### Patches This vulnerability is addressed by validating the `authImage` parameter to ensure it contains only valid OCI image reference characters, rejecting any input containing newlines, whitespace, or other characters that could break YAML syntax.
Patched versions of Rancher include release `v2.14.2`, `v2.13.6`, `v2.12.10`, `v2.11.14` and `v2.10.12`.
### Workarounds If upgrading to a patched version immediately is not feasible, users are encouraged to apply the following workaround:
- Review the `kube-api-auth` DaemonSet: Inspect downstream clusters for the `kube-api-auth` DaemonSet within the `cattle-system` namespace (which targets control-plane nodes). Review this resource configuration carefully for: - Unexpected `command:` or `args:` fields in the container specification. - References to non-standard or suspicious container images. - Any modifications occurring after the initial cluster import. - Validate manifest integrity: Before running `kubectl apply` on any import manifests, verify that the source URLs originate from trusted sources and match expected patterns.
### Credits
This security issue was reported by the following collaborators according to our responsible disclosure policy:
- Radisauskas Arnoldas from NATO and the NATO Cyber Security Centre (NCSC). - Michael Wollner ([`@ibonok`](https://github.com/ibonok)) from Deutsche Telekom AG.

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/rancher — Arbitrary file access via path traversal in Rancher Extensions (CVE-2026-25705)
item.description:
CVE-2026-25705 · CVSS 8.4 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H) · CWE-35
Affected: - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.14.0,<2.14.1 (patched: 2.14.1) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0,<2.13.5 (patched: 2.13.5) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.12.0,<2.12.9 (patched: 2.12.9) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.11.0,<2.11.13 (patched: 2.11.13) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=v2.10.11
---
### Impact
A vulnerability has been identified in [Rancher's Extensions](https://ranchermanager.docs.rancher.com/integrations-in-rancher/rancher-extensions) where malicious code can be injected in Rancher through a path traversal in the `compressedEndpoint` field inside a `UIPlugin` deployment. A malicious UI extension could abuse that to:
- Overwrite Rancher binaries or configuration to inject code. - Write to `/var/lib/rancher/` to tamper with cluster state. - If `hostPath` volumes are mounted, write to the host node filesystem. - Use this issue to chain with other attack vectors.
By default only the administrator can deploy UI extensions, unless permissions are granted to other users. It's always recommended to only install extensions that come from sources trusted by the user.
Please consult the associated [MITRE CAPEC-126 - Technique - Path Traversal](https://capec.mitre.org/data/definitions/126.html) for further information about this category of attack.
### Patches
This vulnerability is addressed by ensuring that:
- The file defined by the UI Plugin CR's `compressedEndpoint` has to be created inside the cache directory and cannot contain `../`. If that is not possible, the installation will fail and the file won't be created. - The icons referenced by Cluster Repos' `index.yaml` file always resolves to a file inside the repository directory.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases v2.14.1, v2.13.5, v2.12.9, v2.11.13.
### Workarounds
There is no workaround. The user must be careful about which UI Plugins they install.

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/rancher — Rancher CLI skips TLS verification on Rancher CLI login command (CVE-2025-67601)
item.description:
CVE-2025-67601 · CVSS 8.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H)
Affected: - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.13.0, <2.13.2 (patched: 2.13.2) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.12.0, <2.12.6 (patched: 2.12.6) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.11.0, <2.11.10 (patched: 2.11.10) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.10.0, <2.10.11 (patched: 2.10.11)
---
### Impact A vulnerability has been identified within Rancher Manager, where using self-signed CA certificates and passing the `-skip-verify` flag to the Rancher CLI login command without also passing the `–cacert` flag results in the CLI attempting to fetch CA certificates stored in Rancher’s setting cacerts. This does not apply to any other commands and only applies to the login command if the `–cacert` flag was not provided.
An attacker with network-level access between the Rancher CLI and Rancher Manager could interfere with the TLS handshake to return a CA they control, despite the use of the `--skip-verify` flag. This may be abused to bypass TLS as a security control. Attackers can also see basic authentication headers in a Man-in-the-Middle due to the lack of TLS enforcement.
Please consult the associated [MITRE ATT&CK - Technique - Man-in-the-Middle](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1557/) for further information about this category of attack.
### Patches This vulnerability is addressed by removing the ability to fetch CA certificates stored in Rancher’s setting cacerts when using the login command. Whenever required, for example when using self-signed certificates, CA certificates have to be explicitly passed with the –cacert flag.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases `v2.13.2`, `v2.12.6`, `v2.11.10`, and `v2.10.11`.
### Workarounds If you can't upgrade to a fixed version, please make sure whenever required, for example when using self-signed certificates, to always explicitly pass CA certificates with the –cacert flag when using the login command.

item.title: [MEDIUM] rancher/rancher — Exposure of sensitive information through audit logs (CVE-2024-58269)
item.description:
CVE-2024-58269 · CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:N/A:N)
Affected: - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.12.0, <2.12.3 (patched: 2.12.3) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.11.0 - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.10.0 - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.9.0
---
### Impact **Note: The exploitation of this issue requires that the malicious user have access to Rancher’s audit log storage.**
A vulnerability has been identified in Rancher Manager, where sensitive information, including secret data, cluster import URLs, and registration tokens, is exposed to any entity with access to Rancher audit logs. This happens in two different ways:
1. Secret Annotation Leakage: When creating Kubernetes Secrets using the `stringData` field, the cleartext value is embedded in the `kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration` annotation. This annotation is included in Rancher audit logs within both the request and response bodies, exposing secret material that should be redacted. 2. Cluster Registration Token Leakage: During the import or creation of downstream clusters (Custom, Imported, or Harvester), Rancher audit logs record full cluster registration manifests and tokens, including: a. Non-expiring import URLs such as `/v3/import/<token>_c-m-xxxx.yaml`. b. Full `kubectl apply` and `curl` commands containing registration tokens and CA checksums. c. Token values associated with cluster registration resources (`clusterRegistrationToken`). d. These tokens are valid until explicitly revoked and can be used to re-register nodes, granting unauthorized cluster access.
An attacker or internal user who gains access to these logs could: - Recover plaintext secret values from annotations. - Use cluster registration tokens or import URLs to re-enroll agents or compromise downstream clusters. - Access clusters that rely on these tokens for authentication, enabling lateral movement.
Please consult the associated [MITRE ATT&CK - Technique - Log Enumeration](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1654/) for further information about this category of attack.
### Patches This vulnerability is addressed by applying redaction to sensitive information that was leaking.
Patched versions of Rancher include release `v2.12.3`.
### Workarounds If the deployment can't be upgraded to a fixed version, users are encouraged to create `AuditPolicies` to redact and filter some of those requests as described in our [documentation](https://ranchermanager.docs.rancher.com/how-to-guides/advanced-user-guides/enable-api-audit-log#audit-log-policies).
The following AuditPolicy can be applied to redact the secrets: ```yaml apiVersion: auditlog.cattle.io/v1 kind: AuditPolicy metadata: name: redactions spec: enabled: true additionalRedactions: - headers: - "Referer" - paths: - "$..metadata.annotations['kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration']" ```
Also consider granting access to Rancher's logs only for trusted users.

item.title: [MEDIUM] rancher/rancher — User retains access to clusters despite Global Role removal (CVE-2023-32199)
item.description:
CVE-2023-32199 · CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:H/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L)
Affected: - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.12.0, <2.12.3 (patched: 2.12.3) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.11.0, <2.11.7 (patched: 2.11.7) - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.10.0 - go/ github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.9.0
---
### Impact A vulnerability has been identified within Rancher Manager, where after removing a custom GlobalRole that gives administrative access or the corresponding binding, the user still retains access to clusters. This only affects custom Global Roles that: - Have a `*` on `*` in `*` rule for resources - Have a `*` on `*` rule for non-resource URLs
For example ```yaml apiVersion: management.cattle.io/v3 kind: GlobalRole metadata: name: custom-admin rules: - apiGroups: - '*' resources: - '*' verbs: - '*' - nonResourceURLs: - '*' verbs: - '*' ```
Specifically: - When a user is bound to a custom admin `GlobalRole`, a corresponding `ClusterRoleBinding` is created on all clusters that binds them to the cluster-admin `ClusterRole`. - When such a `GlobalRole` or the `GlobalRoleBinding` (e.g., when the user is unassigned from this role in UI) is deleted, the `ClusterRoleBinding` that binds them to the cluster-admin ClusterRole stays behind.
This issue allows a user to continue having access to clusters after they have been unassigned from the custom admin global role or the role has been deleted.
Please consult the associated [MITRE ATT&CK - Technique - Account Access Removal](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1531/) for further information about this category of attack.
### Patches This vulnerability is addressed by removing the corresponding `ClusterRoleBindings` whenever the admin `GlobalRole` or its `GlobalRoleBindings` are deleted. Previously orphaned `ClusterRoleBindings` are marked with the annotation `authz.cluster.cattle.io/admin-globalrole-missing=true` and should be deleted manually.
Orphaned ClusterRoleBindings can be listed with: ``` kubectl get clusterrolebinding -o jsonpath='{range .items[?(@.metadata.annotations.authz\.cluster\.cattle\.io/admin-globalrole-missing=="true")]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{end}' ```
Patched versions of Rancher include releases `v2.12.3`, `v2.11.7`.
Complications with the restricted admin functionality prevented the patches from being included in `v2.10` and `v2.9`.
### Workarounds If the deployment can't be upgraded to a fixed version, users are advised to manually identify the orphaned `ClusterRoleBindings` and remove them.

Affected: - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.12.0, <2.12.2 (patched: 2.12.2) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.11.0, <2.11.6 (patched: 2.11.6) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.10.0, <2.10.10 (patched: 2.10.10) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.9.0, <2.9.12 (patched: 2.9.12)

### Impact
A vulnerability has been identified within Rancher Manager where a missing server-side validation on the `.username` field in Rancher can allow users with update permissions on other User resources to cause denial of access for targeted accounts. Specifically:
- Username takeover: A user with permission to update another user’s resource can set its `.username` to "admin", preventing both the legitimate admin and the affected user from logging in, as Rancher enforces uniqueness at login time. - Account lockout: A user with update permissions on the admin account can change the admin’s username, effectively blocking administrative access to the Rancher UI.

### Patches
This vulnerability is addressed by adding a new check in the webhook which blocks modifying usernames after it has been set. If it's empty then the username can be set to a username not already in use, but after that it is immutable.
Patched versions of Rancher include releases v2.12.2, v2.11.6, v2.10.10 and v2.9.12.

item.title: [HIGH] rancher/rancher — Rancher CLI SAML authentication is vulnerable to phishing attacks (CVE-2024-58267)
item.description:
CVE-2024-58267 · CVSS 8.0 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H)
Affected: - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.12.0, <2.12.2 (patched: 2.12.2) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >= 2.11.0, <2.11.6 (patched: 2.11.6) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >= 2.10.0, <2.10.10 (patched: 2.10.10) - go/github.com/rancher/rancher >=2.9.0, <2.9.12 (patched: 2.9.12)
